chapters.title: The Legend of Hundung & The White Cow
chapters.summary: Founding of Hundung village guided by the sacred pregnant cow.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Awo-ayiwui thotchanli: Seiva kachang akha leilaga apha kapha apamli vatuda seinao phanung tharanli Hundung khaung phokna. Kaphung kaphali zatlaga seiva china apam kaphā akha theilaga pamshona; chili seinao phada awo-ayina 'Hundung' (Hungpung) da hoya.
chapters.english_translation: Ancestral lore recounts that the village founders followed a sacred white cow across the hills. Wherever the cow rested upon the fertile plateau, there she gave birth to her calf, and upon that blessed ground the ancient mother-village of Hundung was founded.
comprehension_questions: What animal guided the founders of Hundung?
What does this legend symbolize in Tangkhul pastoralism?

chapters.title: The Two Brothers & Migration to the Hills
chapters.summary: The covenant between elder brother (hills) and younger brother (valley).
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chinaoni khani wui tui: kakhara a kaphungli pamda kakhanao a ngaleili vaipama. Anili khangaran shiyan leiyi: kakhara na kaphungwui theishak kala khuira chili ngaleili phungmiya; kakhanao na ngaleiwui machi kala kachon chili kaphungli phungmiya.
chapters.english_translation: The legend of the two brothers: the elder brother chose the high mountain ridges, while the younger brother cultivated the valley plains. They established a covenant: the elder sent mountain forest produce and honey to the plain, and the younger returned salt and woven cloth.
grammar_points: Reciprocal trade terminology in oral covenants.
comprehension_questions: What goods did the two brothers exchange?
How does this folktale reflect historical trade between hills and valley?

chapters.title: Animal Fables: The Tiger and the Clever Toad
chapters.summary: Wit triumphs over brute force in the forest.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Khawo eina khanei wui khararchan: Khawo khamakang ana ngashida leikha khanei them lak eina makhamatuina. Khawo china 'I eina kaphang ngaroksa!' da kahangli, khanei na awui khamangli khamatuda ngawonshoka. Kong kanda vashung tharan khanei na 'I ashung hairaya!' da kahangli khawo ngacheiseri.
chapters.english_translation: The fable of the tiger and the toad: the mighty tiger boasted of his speed and challenged the toad to a race. The clever toad latched onto the tiger's bushy tail as he leaped across the rocky river, landing first on the bank and declaring victory, teaching that wisdom exceeds brute strength.
grammar_points: Fable dialogue attribution using da kahangli.
comprehension_questions: How did the toad outsmart the tiger?
What is the moral lesson of the fable?

chapters.title: The Story of Huimei and Mountain Spirits
chapters.summary: A brave hunter learns the healing secrets of forest herbs from Kameo spirits.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Huimei kaphungli valaga kameowui tui theiser; khangachei maleila shitsangda ungchan thotna. Kameona ali theishingkhami tarakha thuiya: ngaleiwui themthei eina thingna raha eina mi kakhangasho saikora pangkakhui shiyan.
chapters.english_translation: Huimei, a courageous hunter, encountered the benevolent mountain spirits (Kameo) upon the high ridges. Unafraid, he listened respectfully as they revealed the healing virtues of mountain roots and herbs, returning to his village as a revered traditional healer.
grammar_points: Spiritual respect formulas in oral narratives.
comprehension_questions: What knowledge did Huimei receive from the mountain spirits?
What role do Kameo play in Tangkhul nature philosophy?

chapters.title: The Origin of Rice & The Discovery of Salt
chapters.summary: How hunters discovered saline springs at Marem and the gift of paddy seeds.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Machi eina ma machiwui shiyan: Marem kaphungli tara khamathei machikashak samphangna. Shiva na tara chi mangda leikha sayur tarakhana chili zangda tara kashing mangda leiseri. Chitharan awo-ayina machi tara khumda machi kasa phokna.
chapters.english_translation: The discovery of salt and paddy: ancestral hunters observed wild deer regularly licking certain rocks near Marem. Tasting the spring waters, they discovered natural saline springs and learned to boil the brine in earthenware pots, founding the celebrated salt wells of northern Tangkhul.
grammar_points: Discovery narratives with observation verbs (thei-, samphang-).
comprehension_questions: How was the saline spring discovered?
Why was salt a precious commodity in the hills?

chapters.title: Tales of Morung Bravery & Tricksters
chapters.summary: Feats of strength, archery contests, and humorous trickster narratives in the Longra.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Longrawui yarsona ot kakhayei kasa eina lumlaoda pamshona. Yaron akhana lungrei kahak akha phungshokda awui mathun chitheiya; kateipa china themkhamatha eina malung kharaowa mi akhali ngacheilaka ot kasa themchitheiya.
chapters.english_translation: Youth in the village Morung engaged in athletic competitions and humorous storytelling. One youth proved his strength by lifting heavy megalithic stones, while another displayed quick wit by solving traditional riddles and defusing village rivalries with laughter.
grammar_points: Comparative narrative pairing strength vs intelligence.
comprehension_questions: What competitions were held among morung youths?
Why was storytelling valued in the bachelor dormitory?

chapters.title: Moral Allegories & Customary Wisdom
chapters.summary: Traditional proverbs (Tuingashit) and customary jurisprudence of the council.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul tuingashit: 'Tui kakhayei eina tui khangaran phamei; kazeiram makazamana.' 'Pang eina kasa otna wuklungli karingna.' 'Khaung kaphā khangavawa wui tuiyana.' Mashung kakhayang hi Tangkhul ngashanli khamataiya machutna.
chapters.english_translation: Classical Tangkhul proverbs: 'Reconciliation is sweeter than bitter strife; justice leaves no regret in the afterlife.' 'Labor with one's hands nourishes the soul.' 'A peaceful village reflects the wisdom of its council.' Truthfulness and personal integrity remain the highest virtues of the Tangkhul code.
grammar_points: Aphoristic syntax: parallel clauses without copula.
comprehension_questions: What is the supreme virtue in customary Tangkhul jurisprudence?

lines: CHAPTER 6: TALES OF MORUNG BRAVERY & TRICKSTERS

Youth in the village Morung engaged in athletic competitions and

megalithic stones, while another displayed quick wit by solving
traditional riddles and defusing village rivalries with laughter.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: The Story of Huimei and Mountain Spirits
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Huimei kaphungli valaga kameowui tui theiser; khangachei maleila shitsangda ungchan thotna. Kameona ali theishingkhami tarakha thuiya: ngaleiwui themthei eina thingna raha eina mi kakhangasho saikora pangkakhui shiyan.
excerpts.translation_en: Huimei, a courageous hunter, encountered the benevolent mountain spirits (Kameo) upon the high ridges. Unafraid, he listened respectfully as they revealed the healing virtues of mountain roots and herbs, returning to his village as a revered traditional healer.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: The Origin of Rice & The Discovery of Salt
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Machi eina ma machiwui shiyan: Marem kaphungli tara khamathei machikashak samphangna. Shiva na tara chi mangda leikha sayur tarakhana chili zangda tara kashing mangda leiseri. Chitharan awo-ayina machi tara khumda machi kasa phokna.
excerpts.translation_en: The discovery of salt and paddy: ancestral hunters observed wild deer regularly licking certain rocks near Marem. Tasting the spring waters, they discovered natural saline springs and learned to boil the brine in earthenware pots, founding the celebrated salt wells of northern Tangkhul.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Tales of Morung Bravery & Tricksters
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Longrawui yarsona ot kakhayei kasa eina lumlaoda pamshona. Yaron akhana lungrei kahak akha phungshokda awui mathun chitheiya; kateipa china themkhamatha eina malung kharaowa mi akhali ngacheilaka ot kasa themchitheiya.
excerpts.translation_en: Youth in the village Morung engaged in athletic competitions and humorous storytelling. One youth proved his strength by lifting heavy megalithic stones, while another displayed quick wit by solving traditional riddles and defusing village rivalries with laughter.

excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul tuingashit: 'Tui kakhayei eina tui khangaran phamei; kazeiram makazamana.' 'Pang eina kasa otna wuklungli karingna.' 'Khaung kaphā khangavawa wui tuiyana.' Mashung kakhayang hi Tangkhul ngashanli khamataiya machutna.
excerpts.translation_en: Classical Tangkhul proverbs: 'Reconciliation is sweeter than bitter strife; justice leaves no regret in the afterlife.' 'Labor with one's hands nourishes the soul.' 'A peaceful village reflects the wisdom of its council.' Truthfulness and personal integrity remain the highest virtues of the Tangkhul code.
